notes:
Pass on the fake backend (gate exit 0): evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run helper-wave-1-008) and unreviewed; nothing ran on hardware and no upstream code was imported or executed. The card entry symbol pamila.middle_layer.var_list:MiddleLayerVariableListRO was confirmed at src/pamila/middle_layer/var_list.py:569. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a direct Driver over MiddleLayerVariableListRO instead of OphydDriver, because the entry class is not an ophyd Device and declares no Component signals, so OphydDriver's signal_bindings cannot bind it; the card's cap.device.configure.v1 is used for the local enabled-status write and cap.sensing.read.v1 for reads. The selected class is read-only: its put, set and set_and_wait methods raise ReadOnlyError (src/pamila/middle_layer/var_list.py:582-592), so this package exposes no physical setpoint, motion or actuator and claims no physical e-stop. The e-stop calls disable_parallel_get, the list's own switch; it does not interrupt a member read already running and stops no actuator. R1 is the card's floor; the selected object is observational. The fake holds three placeholder member names, values and units; they are test data, not facts, limits or deployment defaults. The read_channels action groups the upstream get(return_flat=False) slices by member name, so a member with several output channels returns a list under its name; the flat values and value_units state fields keep the upstream flattened order. The upstream PyAT simulator was not used because it needs PyAT and a generated facility configuration, and the clone ships no demo_generated folder; the fake is an in-memory API-preserving stand-in (F0), not a recording. Units are deployment data: src/pamila/facility_configs/loader.py:96-103 builds conversions from repr_units, so value_units reports what each upstream quantity carries. native.py is the hardware factory: it sets PAMILA_FACILITY, loads an operator-supplied generated facility configuration, selects an existing read-only list or builds one from read-only member names, and waits once with the operator timeout. It was never imported or run; no hardware was attached. The loader refuses the hardware backend of an unreviewed model-written package only at R2 and R3, so this R1 package has no such refusal; use it only with a person at the machine. NOT COVERED: the writable MiddleLayerVariable.set_and_wait and MiddleLayerVariableStatusList.set_and_wait paths, the inherited metadata methods get_spec, get_reconstruction_spec, get_spos and get_phys_length (their pydantic/quantity serialization and deployment s-position meaning were not proven), the upstream PyAT simulator, the other entry classes (status list, tree, writable variable), and any generated facility configuration, PV name, engineering unit or numeric setpoint bound. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is the expected warning: the only actuating binding is the boolean enabled-status list, so SAFE-014 has no numeric limit to probe; every other CL3 test passed. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation (right: MiddleLayerVariableListRO is not an ophyd Device and declares no Components, the readiness evidence's reason to block), every fact, native.py and the stop. The R1 pass rested on an invented stop: the read-only list has nothing to stop (its put, set and set_and_wait raise ReadOnlyError, var_list.py:582-592), and the author bound disable_parallel_get, which only decides whether get starts the member PV reads in parallel (var_list.py:170-176, 356-371), as the e-stop to meet the card's R1 floor; that floor comes from a scan-derived cap.device.configure.v1 the class cannot serve, and the configure write was a local enabled-status list. The reviewer made the honest provable subset the package: risk R0 with reads and cap.sensing.read.v1 only; removed the write, the two parallel-get extension actions and the e-stop, rewrote safe_state (unchanged; software latch only) and the docstring, and removed a 'so ...' inference from the device-spec fact (device/base.py:32-40) (driver.py); replaced the write and e-stop cases with a reads-follow-the-list case, a no-write case and a software-latch case (test_driver.py); updated facts.md and the stale R1 sentence of native.py's docstring; regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G3.RISK_FLOOR (card floor R1; stable digest sha256:1a4b05dc9ef2002903cc745266b74177ff2065499a3eae9df7c5740b761a7bf7) and the stock test_gate case fails while blocked; on a scratch copy whose card has risk_floor R0 and cap.sensing.read.v1, G2 to G8 pass (G8 warns SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, as for the apstools exemplar) and all seven package cases pass. Blocked on the card's capability classes (CATALOGUE_GAP: the proposed capability-class override decides them); the author's notes on the write, the parallel-get actions, the e-stop and R1 are superseded. Orchestrator (claude-opus-5-5): the reviewed override in helper-wave-1-routing.json sets the card's capability_classes to cap.sensing.read.v1 (floor R0); with the regenerated card the R0 read-only profile passes the gate, so the package passes instead of blocking on CATALOGUE_GAP. For the human reviewer: Read-only accelerator middle layer: values come from the deployment's facility configuration over EPICS PVs (LIVE) or the PyAT simulator (SIMULATOR). native.py sets the process-wide PAMILA_FACILITY and machine mode, so it needs a dedicated interpreter. On the hardware backend an e-stop reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED (no_stop_path): only the software latch exists and nothing physical is stopped. The card's writable classes (MiddleLayerVariable, MiddleLayerVariableStatusList) write machine setpoints with no stop in the clone and stay out of scope.
